teaser.text: Meta Platforms is mainly an advertising business built on social and messaging apps. A dollar comes in when a business buys access to users, and goes out through the technology, people and physical infrastructure that make that access possible.

paragraphs.text: The weighted price reaches 981.08 in October 2027, a 36% return including dividends. It reaches 1144.01 in October 2028, a 59% return. By October 2029, it reaches 1319.46, an 84% return.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Meta, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Revenue is the main engine. The base case uses growth of 23% in FY2026 and 18% in FY2027, then 16% and 14% as the base becomes larger. The bear path falls from 20% to 6%, while the bull path stays above base from 26% to 20%. First-half revenue was $117,111 million, September guidance was $61–64 billion, and Q2 impressions and average ad prices rose 14% and 12%.

Margins initially absorb the buildout. Base EBITDA margin rises from 44.5% to 48%; bear falls from 43% to 39%; bull rises from 46% to 54%. The starting gap reflects legal costs and infrastructure spending, while the later spread depends on capacity utilization.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Meta?

paragraphs.text: A price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, says how many dollars investors pay for each dollar of annual profit. A trailing P/E uses recorded earnings; a forward P/E uses an estimate, so its denominator may never arrive. EPS means earnings per share, and it can rise through higher profit or fewer shares. Meta’s reported EPS also contains major tax effects: a $15.93 billion non-cash tax charge reduced third-quarter 2025 profit, while an $8.03 billion benefit increased first-quarter 2026 profit. The apparent gap between trailing and forward valuation therefore does not represent pure business growth.

blocks.heading: Does Meta's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash rose in 2025, but purchases of property and equipment rose faster. Calculated free cash flow therefore fell even as sales and operating profit grew. Meta’s own figure is lower because it also deducts principal payments on finance leases, which are another way of paying for assets.

Stock compensation is a real cost to existing owners even when no cash leaves that day. Employees receive valuable shares or share-linked awards, and those claims can dilute other shareholders. Subtracting stock-based pay from free cash flow produces an analytical measure of what owners might more realistically regard as available.

blocks.heading: What is Meta's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Revenue returned to 22.2% growth in 2025. Operating margin slipped to 41.4% from 42.2% in 2024. Meta’s diluted EPS was $23.49 in 2025. Its free cash flow after stock-based pay per share fell to $9.00 from $13.55 in 2024. At $720.89 per share, the valuation is 27.2x trailing P/E. Forward P/E is 21.2x and free cash flow yield is 2.4%. Dividend yield is 0.3%. Net debt remained negative in 2025, but the net-cash cushion narrowed from 2024.

earnings.title: Meta earnings: results and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Meta’s October 21, 2026 results will test $61–64 billion of revenue, $130–145 billion of capital spending, and cash after infrastructure spending.
earnings.opening: Meta’s next results are expected on October 21, 2026. Watch whether infrastructure spending leaves meaningful free cash flow.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Meta’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has Meta guided for the quarter ending September 2026?

paragraphs.text: For the quarter ending September 2026, management forecast revenue of $61–64 billion and assumed a negative 1% currency effect. That means overseas sales will translate into fewer U.S. dollars; it does not mean advertisers are spending less. The basic test is whether advertising demand can keep growing as infrastructure costs rise.

Meta has raised its capital-expenditure forecast twice. The 2026 range began at $115–135 billion, rose to $125–145 billion, and now stands at $130–145 billion. Capital expenditure buys long-lived assets such as servers and data centers, and includes principal repayments on finance leases.

blocks.heading: Has Meta kept its operating promise?

paragraphs.text: Meta completed its efficiency programme, which is evidence that management kept an operating promise. It does not prove that every long-term investment earns enough. Shareholders’ say-on-pay vote is advisory, and Meta holds it every three years, so the board retains wide discretion between votes.

blocks.heading: What has Meta’s revenue and profit trend been over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Profit deteriorated more than gross margin. Operating margin fell because compensation, infrastructure, legal expenses and third-party AI costs increased. Family of Apps operating profit fell to $23,394 million, while Reality Labs lost $4,619 million. The pressure therefore reached the core apps and did not come only from experimental hardware.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Meta’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results, expected on October 28, 2026, should show whether revenue reached guidance, how the legal charge affected profit, and whether infrastructure spending left meaningful free cash flow. Another sales beat would not settle the funding question if little cash remained afterward.
